title: Vitamin D-Dependent Rickets Types 1 and 2: CYP27B1, VDR Mutations and Alopecia
subject: ss-paediatric-endocrinology

steps.say: Vitamin D-dependent rickets type 1A is caused by an inability to bioactivate vitamin D into calcitriol.
steps.tx: Analyze the enzymatic defect and genetics of the **VDDR Type 1A 1-alpha-hydroxylase defect** in young infants. VDDR1A is an autosomal recessive deficiency of renal 25-hydroxyvitamin D 1-alpha-hydroxylase (CYP27B1 on 12q14.1), presenting in the first year of life with severe hypocalcemic tetany, rickets, and normal 25(OH)D but undetectable 1,25(OH)2D.

vis.title: VDDR1A Enzymatic and Biochemical Profile
rows: Presents in first year of life (1 year)
Early hypocalcemic seizures, rickets, growth failure
Adequate substrate from sunlight and diet
Failure of renal conversion to calcitriol
Impaired intestinal absorption and PTH phosphaturia

steps.say: Therapy with physiological calcitriol or alfacalcidol bypasses the 1-alpha-hydroxylase block, rapidly healing rickets.
steps.tx: Administer targeted **Calcitriol physiological replacement in VDDR1A** to restore mineral homeostasis and promote skeletal healing. VDDR1A responds dramatically and completely to physiological doses of oral calcitriol (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3, 0.25-1.0 mcg/day or 20-50 ng/kg/day), bypassing the enzymatic blockade and normalizing serum calcium, alkaline phosphatase, and bone architecture.

vis.title: Calcitriol Bypasses the Renal Hydroxylation Block
edges: Direct calcitriol restores intestinal calcium absorption

steps.say: Vitamin D-dependent rickets type 1B is caused by an inability to perform 25-hydroxylation in the liver.
steps.tx: Differentiate **VDDR Type 1B 25-hydroxylase deficiency** from nutritional vitamin D deficiency. VDDR1B is caused by homozygous mutations in hepatic 25-hydroxylase (CYP2R1 on 11p15.2), characterized by low serum 25(OH)D despite high sunlight/vitamin D exposure, responsive to oral calcifediol or calcitriol. Lifelong therapy restores normal bone architecture, resolves secondary hyperparathyroidism, and optimizes longitudinal adult height potential in growing children.

right.title: VDDR Type 1B (CYP2R1 at 11p15.2)
points: Serum 25(OH)D is low despite high vitamin D intake
Heals with oral calcifediol or calcitriol

steps.say: Vitamin D-dependent rickets type 2A is characterized by end-organ resistance and massively elevated calcitriol levels.
steps.tx: Identify the receptor defect and laboratory hallmarks of **VDDR Type 2A vitamin D receptor mutations** causing hereditary rickets. VDDR2A (hereditary 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D resistant rickets) is caused by end-organ resistance due to mutations in the vitamin D receptor (VDR on 12q13.11), featuring massively elevated serum 1,25(OH)2D (> 150-300 pg/mL).

vis.alt: Young child with severe bowed legs from rickets and complete absence of scalp hair, eyebrows and eyelashes.
vis.caption: Child with vitamin D receptor resistance showing severe rickets together with total alopecia in type 2 disease. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.say: Total alopecia serves as a clinical marker for severe DNA-binding domain mutations in the vitamin D receptor.
steps.tx: Recognize **Total alopecia hallmark in severe VDR defects** as a pathognomonic clinical feature in infants with rickets. Total alopecia (alopecia universalis / absence of scalp hair, eyebrows, and eyelashes) occurs in severe VDDR2A mutants with defective DNA-binding domain, because liganded VDR is required for uncoupled hair follicle cycling.

vis.title: VDR Mutation Severity and Alopecia Correlation

left.title: VDDR2A with Alopecia Universalis
points: Mutations affecting zinc-finger DNA-binding domain or premature stop codons
Complete absence of hair follicle cycling from infancy
Poor skeletal response to oral calcitriol and high calcium doses

right.title: VDDR2A without Alopecia
points: Mutations affecting hormone-binding domain or coactivator interfaces
Preserved hair follicle stem cell function
May respond to pharmacological supra-physiological oral calcitriol

steps.say: Intravenous calcium infusions represent life-saving rescue therapy for children with severe receptor resistance.
steps.tx: Implement long-term **High-dose intravenous calcium rescue in VDDR2A** for children with refractory receptor resistance. Patients with alopecia and severe receptor mutations fail massive oral calcitriol doses; healing of rickets requires long-term continuous central venous intravenous calcium infusions (1000 mg/m²/day elemental calcium) using calcium gluconate over 12-14 hours overnight for several months to years.

vis.title: Intravenous Calcium Rescue Protocol in VDDR2A

nodes.label: Severe VDDR2A with Alopecia (Refractory to Oral Calcitriol)
Placement of Tunneled Central Venous Line
Radiological Healing of Rickets & PTH Normalization

steps.say: Type 2B rickets involves an overexpression of an abnormal nuclear protein that blocks normal receptor binding.
steps.tx: Differentiate the molecular mechanism of **VDDR Type 2B abnormal ribonuclear protein** from primary VDR gene mutations. VDDR2B is caused by overexpression of a dominant-negative ribonuclear protein that binds the vitamin D response element (VDRE), preventing VDR interaction, presenting without alopecia.

vis.title: VDDR2A vs VDDR2B Molecular Lesions
rows: Absent; normal scalp and body hair
Defective VDR protein fails to bind VDRE
Endogenous protein competitively blocks VDRE site
Structurally normal VDR and RXR molecules

steps.say: Gain-of-function CYP3A4 mutations cause rapid catabolism of active vitamin D metabolites.
steps.tx: Recognize the genetic and metabolic etiology of **VDDR Type 3 CYP3A4 gain-of-function** rickets. VDDR3 is caused by a heterozygous gain-of-function recurrent mutation in CYP3A4, which rapidly catabolizes 25(OH)D and 1,25(OH)2D into inactive biliary metabolites, requiring high-dose vitamin D3 to overcome degradation, administered as cholecalciferol.

nodes.label: Rapid Inactivation into Polar Biliary Metabolites

steps.tx: Inside a liver cell, overactive CYP3A4 breaks calcitriol into inactive metabolites, and the wrist film of a clothed child shows cupped, frayed distal ends of the radius and ulna. **VDDR type 3** is a heterozygous gain of function change in CYP3A4 that appears repeatedly in reported cases. The enzyme rapidly destroys both 25 hydroxy vitamin D and 1,25 dihydroxy vitamin D, sending them out as inactive biliary products. High dose cholecalciferol, vitamin D3, is given to outrun that breakdown.
